sections.title: The meeting that ends with nothing
During: stay on it, say who decides
Close: read back, check, write it up

narration: An hour of good discussion.
Then everyone leaves.
What was decided? Who does what?
Nobody can say.
beats.visual_intent: a meeting table sketched with people talking; they leave, the chairs empty, question marks drawn over the table

grounding.claim: a meeting that ends without a clear decision or owner

narration: Say it's Sam's weekly project meeting.
Ask around after, and everyone remembers it differently.
beats.visual_intent: Sam and three teammates drawn; afterwards each has a speech bubble with a different scribble

grounding.claim: Sam's meeting is an illustration
people remember a meeting differently

narration: Three moves fix it.
Before, during, and at the close.
beats.visual_intent: the presenter beside the board as a three-step list appears with empty tick boxes

grounding.claim: name the decision before the meeting
close with a read-back

narration: Before.
Sam's invite says: Pilot update.
That's a subject, not a decision.
beats.visual_intent: the meeting invite drawn as a card with the topic title as its only line; first box on the list highlighted
beats.misconception: an agenda topic is enough to set up a decision

grounding.claim: name the decision before the meeting, in the invite
a topic title only names a subject

narration: Write the decision as a question instead.
Do we ship the pilot in May or June?
Now people come ready to answer.
beats.visual_intent: the topic title on the invite is crossed out and the question is written in its place

grounding.claim: phrase the decision as a question so people know what to answer

narration: Invite whoever owns that decision,
and whoever it can't be made without.
Everyone else gets the notes.
beats.visual_intent: the invite list of faces is trimmed to the owner and the needed inputs; the rest get an envelope for the notes

grounding.claim: invite the owner and those whose input it needs
people who only need the result get the written summary

narration: During.
Open by saying the question again.
A side topic comes up? Park it,
in a corner of the board, with a name.
beats.visual_intent: Sam at the board points to the question; a side topic bubble floats in and is written into a box drawn in the board's corner, with a name beside it

grounding.claim: restate the decision before discussion starts
a parking lot is a visible list of off-topic items, such as a corner of the board
name someone to pick each parked item up

narration: Then say how it's decided, and who calls it.
Here, Priya decides after hearing the group.
beats.visual_intent: Priya is circled as the one who calls it, the group's arrows pointing to her; the second step gets its tick

grounding.claim: make clear how the decision will be made
make clear who makes the decision
Priya as decision owner is an illustration

narration: At the close, read each decision back.
What, who owns it, by when.
People can still correct it in the room.
beats.visual_intent: Sam reads from the board; the three parts of a decision are underlined one by one as they are spoken

grounding.claim: close by reading back each decision with owner and due date so people can correct it

narration: Quick check. Which line is a decision?
Discussed the pilot timeline.
Or: pilot ships in June, Priya, by Friday.
beats.visual_intent: two lines of notes side by side on the board, nothing marked yet

recall.tempting_wrong: the first names the subject but records only a topic discussed

beats.delivery: a short pause after the question

grounding.claim: a topic line is not a decision; a decision states what, owner and date
the two note lines are illustrations

narration: The second.
The first only names a topic.
A decision says what, who, and by when.
beats.visual_intent: a cross drawn on the first line and a tick on the second; the second line's three parts are labelled
beats.misconception: a topic discussed in the notes means something was decided
beats.delivery: slower on what makes a line a decision

grounding.claim: a recorded decision states what, who and by when

narration: Then send it in writing, ideally the same day,
to everyone there and anyone affected.
One version of the meeting.
beats.visual_intent: the decision lines fold into an email that flies out to the team; the mismatched speech bubbles from b02 become one

grounding.claim: send decisions in writing soon after, ideally the same day, to attendees and anyone affected
everyone checks the same list

narration: Same team, same hour.
Now it ends with decisions, owners and dates,
read back and sent.
beats.visual_intent: Sam's meeting table again, ending on a short list of decisions with names and dates; all three steps ticked

grounding.claim: decisions read back with owner and date
sent in writing

narration: Before your next meeting,
rewrite the agenda's first line as a question.
Name it, steer it, read it back.
beats.visual_intent: a blank agenda with a question mark on its first line; the three-part rule written underneath

grounding.claim: name the decision in the agenda before the meeting
phrase it as a question
